question: How do the declared local encounter and transport conditions evolve over a broad range of encounter prefactors, with the same reservoir aperture and explicit stoichiometry?
role: F, prospective conditions map; no desired morphology is specified
reuse: Exact existing N24/T300/same-seed/same-physical-parameter discovery histories are linked with hashes, never rerun or counted twice. A mathematically equivalent sparse proposal scheduler may be used for new points only after independent validation.

numerical_acceleration.reason: A fuel or waste neighbor cannot also be a B neighbor. At given nB, sample a neighbor uniformly from the z-nB non-B neighbors and use conditional reaction coefficient k_cond=k_raw*(z-nB)/z. The maximum k_cond supplies the bound. Actual rate for each allowed occupied fuel pair remains k_cond/(z-nB)=k_raw/z, exactly the original law. nB=z permits no fuel encounter.
numerical_acceleration.validation_before_research: grand-canonical/source/closed balances plus an isolated two-state pair with nB=2: equilibrium probabilities AND temporal autocorrelation must match exact transition rates; deterministic repeats and overwrite protection

observations: Same original density widths/thresholds, local reaction bins, x profiles, source currents, state histories and medium-entropy ledger. All points/seeds retained. No new success threshold.
interpretation: The completed60 runs show that transport geometry and actual finite fuel matter; single-path controls still assemble without sustained cycling.
